bull.b: FDA IND clearance for VY1706 materially de-risks the preclinical-to-clinic transition and paves the way for clinical proof-of-concept. Over 2-6 months this enables enrollment, data generation and potential milestone triggers or partnering discussions that can transform capital needs and strategic optionality.

Six-month GLP non-human primate data showing broad CNS delivery, durable tau lowering up to 75% and favorable tolerability indicate strong translational potential of Voyager's vector and capsid platform. This durable evidence reduces biological risk and strengthens the company's competitive position in CNS gene therapy.

Approval to nearly double authorized shares plus re-election of directors signals shareholder endorsement and provides tangible capital-raising flexibility. Over months this structural change preserves the company's ability to access equity or transact strategically to fund clinical programs and partnerships without governance disruption.

bear.b: Operating cash flow swung from positive to a -$154M TTM outflow, reflecting rapid burn tied to clinical and R&D activity. Persistently negative cash generation over months erodes runway, forces dilutive financings or costly partnerships, and increases execution risk for multi-year CNS programs.

Revenue plunged from $250M to $34.5M TTM and margins moved from profit to sizable losses, indicating reduced partner/license income. Structurally lower contract revenue undermines internal funding capacity for trials, increasing dependency on external capital and partnership milestones to sustain programs.

Shareholder equity has roughly halved over recent periods, shrinking the balance-sheet buffer. While leverage remains moderate, the declining capital base reduces financial flexibility, raises dilution risk on future financings, and could weaken negotiating leverage with partners or creditors over the next several quarters.
